verdict.rationale: Auth0 documents a Client Credentials flow built for machine-to-machine applications such as CLIs, daemons and backend services. Applications authenticate with a Client ID and Client Secret and receive an Access Token with no user involved, and M2M permissions can be scoped. Auth0 also markets a unique digital identity for each agent. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the M2M flow, and documentation of credential issuance and rotation details (e.g., secret rotation, private-key JWT options).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue machine-to-machine credentials (client-credentials flow) so backend services and agents authenticate without a human in the loop

citations.quote: This flow is best suited for Machine-to-Machine (M2M) applications, such as CLIs, daemons, or backend services, because the system must authenticate and authorize the application instead of a user.
Applications authenticate themselves to Auth0 via their Client Id and Client Secret. Auth0 verifies the information and responds with an Access Token.
Handle authorization using scopes and granular permissions, whether it's for first-party apps, third-party integrations, or Machine-to-Machine communications.
Give each agent a unique digital identity for more secure access to APIs, apps, and MCP servers.
